svg.title: Sell a Measured Scope, Then Prove Delivery
svg.desc: diagram id: diag-01-measured-scope-to-renewal; chart type: process_flow; title: Sell a Measured Scope, Then Prove Delivery; subtitle: Five operating stages for recurring commercial and medical janitorial contracts.; chapter number: 1; epistemic tag: operating_framework; assumptions note: Recognized operator revenue is earned cleaning contract revenue. Customer building value, tenant sales, and proposed contract value are excluded. Higher revenue requires additional paid productive crew hours, higher realized pricing, or both.; caption: The workflow connects the bid estimate to actual paid hours, documented service quality, invoicing, and renewal pricing.; stages: label: Qualify the route; value: Confirm buyer, location, frequency, and payment terms; numeric value: 1.0; detail: Record the facility manager, purchasing authority, building address, service windows, invoice requirements, and travel time from existing stops. Flag customer concentration before adding a large account.; label: Measure the scope; value: Inventory cleanable area and task-level service frequencies; numeric value: 2.0; detail: Walk the site with the buyer; count restrooms, fixtures, floor types, touchpoints, waste stations, and restricted rooms. Distinguish usable cleanable area from leased area and separate periodic floor work from nightly service.; label: Price paid capacity; value: Convert observed production into fully loaded labor costs; numeric value: 3.0; detail: Estimate area tasks as square feet divided by task-specific ISSA production-rate references. Add fixture tasks, setup, paid travel, inspections, breaks where required, and rework. Validate with a timed pilot and include payroll burden, overtime, supplies, overhead, and target profit.; label: Mobilize and inspect; value: Assign qualified labor and capture completed-task evidence; numeric value: 4.0; detail: Use Swept or a comparable scheduling and inspection system to assign employee work, record exceptions, and track corrective actions. Independently operated subcontractors deliver contracted outcomes under their own lawful methods.; label: Bill and renew; value: Reconcile accepted services, collection timing, and account margin; numeric value: 5.0; detail: Issue QuickBooks invoices against contracted service periods and approved extras. Compare actual hours with the bid weekly; correct scope creep, repeated callbacks, and slow payment before the next renewal.

rect.title: label: Bill and renew; value: Reconcile accepted services, collection timing, and account margin; numeric value: 5.0; detail: Issue QuickBooks invoices against contracted service periods and approved extras. Compare actual hours with the bid weekly; correct scope creep, repeated callbacks, and slow payment before the next renewal.

text.title: Issue QuickBooks invoices against contracted service periods and approved extras. Compare actual hours with the bid weekly; correct scope creep, repeated callbacks, and slow payment before the next renewal.

Assumptions: Recognized operator revenue is earned cleaning contract revenue. Customer building value, tenant sales, and proposed contract value are excluded. Higher revenue requires additional paid productive crew hours, higher realized pricing, or both.
